description: Feature flag traffic and evaluations by flag, decision and Sigil reason, evaluation latency, errors and policy reloads, the Rust process, and k6 load measurements, across Mimir metrics, Tempo traces, Loki logs and Pyroscope profiles. Flag filters the evaluation and trace panels; Load run filters the k6 panels.

panels.description: 1 while Alloy's scrape of featuregate's /metrics succeeds.
panels.title: Service up

panels.description: Flags with a compiled policy in the flag directory, the ones OFREP answers for. A flag file without a policy, or whose policy failed to compile, is not served.
panels.title: Flags served

panels.description: Flag evaluations answered, from single and bulk OFREP requests alike.
panels.title: Evaluations / second

panels.description: Share of evaluations that failed and were answered fail-closed (disable, reason ERROR). Anything above zero deserves a look at Errors by kind.
panels.title: Error ratio

panels.description: Reloads in the selected range that failed, and kept the last-known-good policies because the directory didn't compile or broke a guardrail.
panels.title: Failed reloads

panels.description: 1 while /readyz answers 200: every flag policy compiled and the evaluation pool is up.
panels.title: Ready

panels.description: The featuregate build Alloy is scraping.
panels.title: Version

panels.description: 1 when the Sigil module loaded precompiled, so startup takes milliseconds. 0 means this start compiled it, which takes seconds: fuel metering is on, or the binary was built without the precompiled feature.
panels.title: Precompiled engine

panels.description: OFREP and management requests per second by route template, so unknown paths can't blow up the label.
panels.title: Requests by route

panels.description: Responses by status code: 304 is a bulk evaluation the client's ETag still matched, 404 an unknown flag, 400 a bad context.
panels.title: Requests by status

panels.description: p95 and p99 of request duration per route template, measured inside featuregate; k6 below measures from the client.
panels.title: HTTP latency by route
Evaluations by flag, decision and reason

panels.description: Evaluations per second for each flag. Flag is a bounded label: requests for flags that don't exist count as -.
panels.title: Evaluations by flag

panels.description: What Sigil decided: enable or disable.
panels.title: Evaluations by decision

panels.description: The reason of each decision: rollout and targeted and enterprise and beta_tester enable; kill_switch, region_not_ready and not_rolled_out disable. A kill_switch or region_not_ready line is the platform guardrail firing.
panels.title: Evaluations by Sigil reason

panels.description: The fraction of each flag's evaluations that enabled it: the flag's effective rollout as served, not as configured.
panels.title: Enabled share by flag

panels.description: Sigil evaluation time inside the WebAssembly engine, per flag's policy, without HTTP handling. The deadline is the service's FEATUREGATE_EVALUATION_TIMEOUT.
panels.title: Evaluation latency

panels.description: Evaluations answered fail-closed, by what went wrong: timeout, conflict, assertion, runtime, stopped or internal. Each one is also an evaluation with reason ERROR.
panels.title: Errors by kind

panels.description: Reloads by result: loaded swapped a new set of compiled flag policies in, unchanged found the directory as it was, failed kept the last good ones.
panels.title: Policy reloads

panels.description: Flags with a compiled policy over time, and the content digest of the policy bundle being served (1 while it is the one in use): a new digest line after a reload is a bundle that loaded. A drop in flags means a flag's policy was removed or stopped compiling.
panels.title: Flags served and bundle

panels.description: Evaluation instances replaced because they trapped, timed out or were killed (every one is an incident worth a trace), instances being rebuilt right now, and HTTP requests being served right now.
panels.title: Pool replacements, rebuilds and requests in flight

panels.description: Names in FEATUREGATE_KILLED_FLAGS that no loaded flag has. Above zero means a kill switch is set for a flag that does not exist, most likely a typo, so the flag you meant to switch off is still on.
panels.title: Kill-switch names without a flag

panels.description: CPU seconds per second (cores) and resident set size. Memory that only grows across a soak test is a leak in the instance pool or the WebAssembly memory.
panels.title: CPU and resident memory

panels.description: Tokio workers, blocking-pool threads running evaluations, and open sockets and files.
panels.title: Threads and open file descriptors

panels.description: Requests per second k6 sent, by load run.
panels.title: k6 · request rate

panels.description: Share of evaluations whose value, variant, reason or metadata differed from the expectation, by scenario. Must stay at zero, reloads included.
panels.title: k6 · incorrect answers

panels.description: p95 as the client saw it, by request kind.
panels.title: k6 · HTTP p95 by request

panels.description: p99 as the client saw it, by request kind.
panels.title: k6 · HTTP p99 by request

panels.description: Flag evaluations k6 verified, by the value the service answered.
panels.title: k6 · evaluations by value

panels.description: Reloads k6 sent by answer status: 200 swapped, 500 is run.sh's broken document being refused while the last good policies keep serving.
panels.title: k6 · reloads under load

panels.description: Requests k6 meant to send and couldn't because every virtual user was busy, and the virtual users active.

panels.title: k6 · dropped iterations and VUs

panels.description: Traces of featuregate.evaluate spans, one per flag evaluation, for the selected flags. Open one to see the flag, Sigil's decision and reason, and OFREP's reason, then use its Logs link to open the log line in Loki.
panels.title: Evaluation traces · Tempo

panels.description: One line per evaluation: the flag, the decision and its reason. Expand a line and follow View trace. Explore logs includes access logs and errors too.
panels.title: Evaluation logs · Loki

panels.description: CPU time of the whole process over the dashboard time range, sampled by pprof-rs: HTTP handling, evaluations on the blocking pool, and the WebAssembly engine's compiled code. Click a stack frame to focus it. Profiles upload every 10 seconds.
panels.title: CPU profile · Pyroscope
